item.title: Artificial Intelligence and Marketing: Rethinking Knowledge through a Human-in-the-Loop Perspective
item.content:encoded:
Peilin Phua, Adelaide University

Zachary William Anesbury, Adelaide University

Michael Mehmet, University of Wollongong

Kristina Klein, University of Bremen

This special issue examines how artificial intelligence is reshaping marketing knowledge production, with a focus on the Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) perspective. Rather than emphasizing AI's efficiency and predictive capabilities, the collection investigates what these technological shifts mean for how marketing knowledge is generated, validated, and understood. HITL practices ensure that human judgment remains active and accountable throughout the knowledge production process.

The special issue draws on the journal's tradition of exploring how marketing knowledge is produced through practice rather than merely discovered. Contributors are invited to examine the relationship between human and AI agency in knowledge generation, including questions about expertise, rigour, and trustworthiness when AI tools are involved in research and practice. The collection welcomes conceptual, empirical, methodological, and critical perspectives on AI's broader disciplinary and institutional implications in marketing.

Appel publié par Journal of Marketing Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Conceptual and theoretical work examining HITL and how AI-assisted research tools shape marketing knowledge and markets
  • Socio-material and more-than-human perspectives on human–AI collaboration in marketing research and practice
  • Methodological innovation in AI-assisted qualitative research, including netnography, discourse analysis, and ethnographic approaches
  • Critical examination of how AI shapes the labour, expertise, and interpretive practices of marketing researchers and practitioners
  • The design and evaluation of HITL systems in marketing analytics, consumer research, and decision-making, including how such systems shape knowledge production and use
  • The use of AI for synthetic data generation or research alternatives, examining human oversight and its implications for knowledge claims
  • Ethical and societal implications of AI in marketing knowledge production
  • Research revisiting established marketing findings using AI-assisted methods (e.g., replication and generalisation across contexts), evaluating how these approaches contribute to the validation, interpretation, and enactment of marketing knowledge

Timeline

  • March 1, 2027: Manuscript deadline

item.title: Cripping the Market: Toward Further Advances in Disability and Consumption Research
item.content:encoded:
Anthony Beudaert, University Toulouse – Jean Jaurès

Jean-Philippe Nau, University of Lorraine

Anna Schneider-Kamp, Syddansk Universitet

Søren Askegaard, Syddansk Universitet

This special issue addresses disability as a central dimension of contemporary markets and consumption. Building on recent scholarship including a previous JMM special issue on the disabling marketplace and the Cripped Marketing Manifesto, the collection seeks to move beyond foundational work on marketplace exclusion toward deeper investigations of embodied, temporal, and affective aspects of disabled market life. The issue invites contributions exploring what remains theoretically, methodologically, and practically unsaid about how disability reshapes our understanding of markets themselves.

Appel publié par Journal of Marketing Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Phenomenological and embodied accounts of impairment in consumption experiences
  • Chronic illness, pain, and fatigue as market experiences
  • Time, rhythm, and slowness in disabled temporalities and consumer culture
  • Invisible impairments and misrecognition in market encounters
  • Caregivers, support networks, and distributed consumption practices
  • Autonomy, dependence, and interdependence in market participation
  • Disability, aging, and embodied vulnerability across the life course
  • Markets for aging bodies and assistive technologies
  • Progressive conditions and shifting market participation over time
  • Disability in the Anthropocene and environmental justice
  • Capitalist ableism and market logics producing disability
  • Accessibility barriers in retail, design, tourism, transport, and digital services
  • Dis/abling infrastructures in built and digital environments
  • Algorithmic discrimination and the platform economy
  • Artificial intelligence and automation for consumers with disabilities
  • Representation and commodification of disability in advertising and media
  • Market activism and disability justice movements
  • Policy and governance frameworks for accessible markets
  • Historical and genealogical studies of accessible markets and assistive industries
  • Medico-social sector as a market and commercialization of care
  • Crip theory as a lens for consumer research
  • Neurodiversity, diagnosis, and market effects
  • Critique of normative consumer agency and the able-bodied consumer subject
  • Intersectionality in disability and consumption
  • Postcolonial and decolonial approaches to disability and markets
  • Posthumanism and bodily augmentation in disability contexts
  • New materialisms and assemblage approaches to embodied market relations
  • Participatory and co-productive research methods in disability contexts
  • Cripistemology as methodology centered on disabled lived experience
  • Arts-based and alternative formats for knowledge-making
  • Ethics, positionality, and politics of knowledge production in disability research
  • Market activism as research practice
  • Accessible dissemination and knowledge translation

Timeline

  • May 17, 2027: Manuscript submission deadline

item.title: Literary Perspectives on Marketing
item.content:encoded:
Jonatan Södergren, University of Bristol

Anthony Patterson, Lancaster University

Cele Otnes, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

This special issue seeks to establish literature as a valuable resource for marketing and consumer research. While marketing scholars have long studied stories and narratives, literary texts and literary theory remain underutilized in the field. The editors invite researchers to explore how novels, poetry, drama, and other literary forms can deepen our understanding of consumer behavior, brands, and markets in ways that complement traditional empirical approaches.

The issue welcomes three main types of contributions: studies using literary texts as empirical material to examine consumer culture; scholarship applying literary theory concepts to marketing phenomena; and reflections on literary methods and epistemologies in consumer research. Additionally, the editors invite work on how literature itself is marketed and consumed, including phenomena like BookTok, and submissions that experiment with literary and creative writing forms as modes of scholarly contribution when integral to the research.

Appel publié par Journal of Marketing Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • What insights can fiction provide for understanding contemporary consumer culture and marketing phenomena that remain inaccessible through conventional empirical approaches?
  • How can specific concepts from literary theory be used as analytical tools for understanding contemporary consumer culture and branding practices?
  • What epistemological assumptions are challenged when novels and other fictional texts are treated as legitimate data sources for understanding consumer culture?
  • How can narratological concepts deepen our understanding of consumer journeys and marketing experiences?
  • How do actors across the book industry (publishers, authors, booksellers) deploy marketing activities to increase the demand for literary works?
  • What role does BookTok and other digital trends play in driving literary consumption?
  • How can creative writing practices be integrated into consumer research?
  • What forms of scholarly contribution become possible when researchers adopt literary or experimental modes of writing?

Timeline

  • June 7, 2027: Manuscript deadline

item.title: Brand Activism at a Crossroads: New Theoretical and Empirical Horizons in Marketing and Society
item.content:encoded:
Antonella Cammarota, International University of Monaco

Jessica Vredenburg, Auckland University of Technology

Benjamin Rosenthal, Getulio Vargas Foundation

Brand activism has evolved into a mainstream corporate practice where companies and executives publicly engage with controversial socio-political issues. While existing literature has explored authenticity, ideology, and corporate strategies in brand activism, there remains a significant gap regarding its broader social and transformative impacts. The phenomenon has expanded across diverse contexts including non-profits, universities, CEOs, and consumers, and is studied in B2B markets, the luxury sector, and globally.

Recent developments suggest that brand activism is undergoing significant transformation. Since late 2024, many major corporations have withdrawn from diversity and inclusion commitments, scaled back activist visibility on social media, and reduced socio-political content. This shift, driven by rising populism, geopolitical conflicts, and societal polarisation, highlights a critical disconnect between existing theoretical frameworks and evolving real-world practices that scholars struggle to capture adequately.

Appel publié par Journal of Marketing Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Changes in Brand Activism Strategies – Is brand activism taking a new form? Are we witnessing the rise of less visible, more strategic, or quieter modes of activism? How do activist brands act in the current landscape?
  • Emerging Brand Activist Contexts – How, and to what extent, does brand activism manifest across different political, cultural, and geographical contexts? Particular attention is invited to the Global South and emerging markets, where civil liberties, media pluralism, or legal protections for civil rights may be limited or contested.
  • Institutional Actors as Activist Agents – What happens when universities, public institutions, public figures, or cultural organisations engage in activist practices? How do these actors influence public discourse, shape political debate, or redefine the boundaries of market responsibility?
  • The Transformative Effect of Brand Activism – Can marketing-driven activism lead to lasting social change, or is it ultimately limited to symbolic gestures and market-oriented performance goals?
  • International and Transnational Dimensions of Activism – How does activism unfold across national borders, global supply chains, and international institutions? What new conditions arise when brand activism is framed as a systemic, transnational commitment?
  • Backlash, Culture War, and Polarisation – How brand activism is affected when social and institutional risks emerge, corporate activism provokes ideological resistance, public fatigue, or consumer boycotts? How has the context of rising populism affected the conditions for brand activism?
  • Consumer Activism and Spaces of Expression – Has consumer activism changed? If so, how do activist consumers influence brand strategies, communication, and positioning? How do new forms of digital and/or offline spaces affect how consumer activists express their demands, critiques, or support? Are there changes in the relationships between brands and consumer activists?
  • Authenticity and Consumer Activism - How can we critically differentiate between authentic brand activism and opportunistic appropriation of activist discourse? Have consumers' understandings of authentic brand activism changed amid current shifts in the sociocultural context?
  • Artificial Intelligence and Activist Contents – How is artificial intelligence transforming the creation, personalisation, and dissemination of activist messages? What ethical, moral, and authenticity-related concerns arise when activism is mediated by machine-created content?
  • Shifting Channels of Activist Communication – To what extent has sociopolitical pressure prompted a shift in activist communication from open, accessible platforms - such as social media - to more niche, closed (not public) or offline spaces? What are the implications of this relocation of activism visibility and audience engagement regarding brand activism practices and social impact?
  • Activism and the Depoliticisation of Society – What are the potential connections between brand activism and the depoliticisation of society? Does brand activism foster genuine political engagement and collective mobilisation, or does it risk causing activism fatigue, depoliticising conflict and reinforcing dominant ideologies? How can we critically assess the boundaries between symbolic engagement and meaningful transformation?
  • Measuring Systemic Impact – How can we assess the broader societal effects of brand activism beyond corporate performance indicators or consumer responses? What critical or participatory methodologies are needed to evaluate systemic change?

Timeline

  • September 30, 2026: Manuscript deadline

item.title: Marketing in a Divisive World: The Role of Political Forces in Shaping Marketing and Consumption
item.content:encoded:
Hanna Reinikainen, University of Helsinki

Essi Pöyry, University of Helsinki

Jason Weismueller, University of Western Australia

Rory Mulcahy, University of the Sunshine Coast

Political divisions are reshaping marketing and consumption as brands face mounting pressure to respond to geopolitical conflicts, populist movements, and ideological tensions. Divisive politics no longer remains confined to formal institutions but permeates lifestyle choices, cultural narratives and consumption practices, compelling brands to navigate scrutiny not only for what they communicate but also for what they remain silent about.

Multiple pathways allow political forces to influence marketing systems, including brand activism and consumer responses to sociopolitical positioning, political ideology affecting consumer preferences and attachment, and boycott or buycott movements impacting marketplace outcomes. Digital infrastructures and social media influencers increasingly amplify political signals while spreading misinformation, creating complex dynamics where brand silence itself becomes a political statement carrying strategic risks.

Appel publié par Journal of Marketing Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Political ideologies, identities and lifestyle politics: How do political forces shape consumption choices, brand perceptions, media use and information processing?
  • Explicit political stances, silence and neutrality in brand communication: When, why, and how does taking a political stance, or the refusal to engage in such, generate support, scepticism, backlash or disengagement?
  • Consumer activism, boycotts, buycotts and cancel culture: How do consumers mobilise for or against brands, and what determines escalation, forgiveness or longer-term market consequences?
  • Influencers, creators and political-commercial hybrids: How do influencers, celebrities, and other intermediaries blur the boundaries between promotion, identity politics, advocacy and civic participation?
  • Digital platforms, algorithms and misinformation: How do platform design, governance, recommendation systems and mis/disinformation shape exposure to and responses to political marketplace content?
  • Race, nationalism, populism and anti-DEI movements: How do contested political projects reshape inclusion, exclusion, legitimacy and representation in markets?
  • Ethics, responsibility and governance: What normative, regulatory and strategic questions arise when market actors seek to leverage political issues or influence public discourse?
  • Methodological and theoretical innovation: What new concepts, frameworks and methods are needed to study politics in contemporary marketing and consumption?

Timeline

  • February 1, 2027: Manuscript deadline

item.title: The Disinformation Economy: Digital Markets of Influence, Conflict, and Polarization
item.content:encoded:

Appel publié par Journal of Marketing Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Whether and how programmatic advertising funds fake news
  • How do the recommender algorithms amplify incendiary content
  • How can AI-generated content be used to spread disinformation
